descriptionChirho: A beloved person, romantic lover or darling, used extensively in Song of Solomon; cross-linguistically rendered as spa 'amado', hin 'प्रीतम/प्रेमी', arb 'دُود/حَبِيب', kor '사랑하는 자', swa 'mpenzi', consistently distinct from the kinship term 'uncle'.

A paternal uncle or close male kinship relation; cross-linguistically rendered as spa 'tío', hin 'चाचा', arb 'عَمّ', kor '삼촌', swa 'mjomba/ami/baba mdogo', clearly distinguished from the romantic 'beloved' sense across all languages.

Abstract noun denoting love or caresses (often plural דּוֹדִים), rendered as spa 'amores', hin 'प्रेम', arb 'حُبّ', kor '사랑', swa 'upendo'; distinct from the personal 'beloved/lover' sense in that it refers to the emotion or act rather than the person.
